subject.title: Feature: Webchat / Control UI inline button support (buttons parameter, callback RPC, capabilities config)

question: Should WebChat inline interactions use shared `presentation` typed actions with a new authenticated `chat.callback` RPC, and should any capability gate be config-backed or always capability-discovered?
rationale: The first implementation would define public Gateway protocol, Control UI behavior, callback authorization semantics, and possibly a replacement for a retired WebChat config surface.

options.title: Presentation plus authenticated RPC
options.body: Use shared presentation typed actions, add a scoped authenticated `chat.callback` RPC, defer webhook routing, and explicitly decide whether a WebChat capability config exists.

options.title: Split contract before UI
options.body: Approve only the schema/RPC/auth contract first, then implement Control UI rendering and click states in a follow-up issue or PR.

options.title: Defer interactive WebChat
options.body: Keep WebChat text-only for now and route broader browser interaction work through the larger WebUI reactions and feedback tracker.

recommendation.title: Presentation plus authenticated RPC
recommendation.body: Use shared presentation typed actions, add a scoped authenticated `chat.callback` RPC, defer webhook routing, and explicitly decide whether a WebChat capability config exists.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest inspected history on typed presentation actions and shared interactive rendering contracts that the recommended design would reuse.
